prompt: A model fails a threshold but is very cheap. What is it?

choices.text: A good candidate if the saving is large enough
choices.why: No price makes up for a failed threshold.

choices.text: Not a candidate
choices.why: Right. It leaves the list before anything is ranked.

choices.text: A candidate for the batch tier only
choices.why: Batch is a price, not a way around a threshold.

choices.text: The default, until a better one is measured
choices.why: A model that cannot do the job is never the default.

prompt: Match each criterion, as ana uses it, to its kind.

pairs.left: Customer e-mail may go to this provider
Price per month for the workload
At least 35 of 40 cases sorted correctly

pairs.right: Quality above the floor, a trade-off

right_distractors: A score to add to the others

prompt: Why does the method filter before it ranks, rather than scoring every model on all five criteria and adding up?

choices.text: A sum lets a low price buy back a failed requirement
choices.why: Right. A threshold is pass or out; adding it to a score hides a failure behind a bargain.

choices.text: Adding up is slower to compute
choices.why: It is no slower; it is wrong.

choices.text: The five criteria are measured in different currencies
choices.why: Units can be converted; the problem is that some criteria are not scores at all.

choices.text: Ranking is only allowed after lesson 5
choices.why: Order matters for a reason, not by rule.

prompt: Which of ana's requirements can the sheet check directly?
hint: `sheet pick` has a flag for it.

choices.text: That the model writes natural Portuguese
choices.why: That is a measurement on her cases.

choices.text: That the terms allow processing customer e-mail
choices.why: Terms are documents to read, provider by provider.

choices.text: That it sorts 35 of 40 cases correctly
choices.why: That is lesson 5's measurement.

choices.text: A window of at least 32,000 tokens
choices.why: Right: --min-window.

prompt: Adding a ceiling of $1 per million input tokens to `sheet pick` left 893 entries, the cheapest of them unfamiliar. What does section 03 take from that?
hint: Was the ceiling one of her thresholds?

choices.text: That the cheapest entries are the best value
choices.why: Nothing about them has been measured.

choices.text: That a preference used as a filter narrows the wrong way
choices.why: Right. Price is a trade-off, ranked after the thresholds.

choices.text: That the sheet's prices are wrong
choices.why: Unusual prices are a reason to check, not proof of an error.

choices.text: That a lower ceiling would give a better short list
choices.why: Tightening the wrong filter makes it worse.

prompt: Why does ana narrow 1,617 entries to a short list by judgement rather than by a further filter?
hint: What do the remaining requirements need?

choices.text: Because filters are slow on large sheets
choices.why: Speed is not the issue.

choices.text: Because judgement is more accurate than measurement
choices.why: The short list only chooses what to measure; measurement decides.

choices.text: The rest are measurements, and 1,617 is too many to measure
choices.why: Right. Judgement picks several candidates; measuring corrects a bad pick.

choices.text: Because the sheet has no field for Portuguese, and adding one to it is forbidden
choices.why: Nothing forbids it; it would still not measure quality.

prompt: Within one model family, which ordering does section 04 call reliable?

choices.text: The larger model is better on hard tasks
choices.why: Right. Across families the ordering does not hold.

choices.text: The newest model is the cheapest
choices.why: Newness and price are not tied.

choices.text: The smallest model has the largest window
choices.why: Window size is set per model, not by size.

choices.text: Its leaderboard rank predicts your task
choices.why: Leaderboards measure somebody else's tasks.

prompt: Which statement of a quality threshold can be checked?
hint: A number on a set of cases.

choices.text: The model must be accurate
choices.why: Accurate how often, on what?

choices.text: The model must be among the top ten on a public leaderboard this month
choices.why: That checks a leaderboard, not the task.

choices.text: At least 35 of 40 sorted as a person sorted them
choices.why: Right: a number, on named cases, against a person's answers.

choices.text: Better than the model we used last year
choices.why: Better by how much, on what?

prompt: A wrong order number in an extraction sends the wrong refund; a wrong label costs a minute of moving an e-mail. What follows for the two floors?
hint: A floor is chosen from the cost of a mistake.

choices.text: Both floors should be equal, so the comparison is fair
choices.why: Different costs of error justify different floors.

choices.text: Extraction's floor is higher
choices.why: Right, and one model can pass one task and fail the other.

choices.text: Sorting's floor is higher, because it runs more often
choices.why: Frequency matters, but each sorting error is cheap.

choices.text: Neither needs a floor once a person reviews the output
choices.why: Review costs time, and the floor decides whether the tool saves any.

prompt: Why did caching cut Claude Haiku's drafting bill from $72.72 to $18.72?
hint: What is the same on every request?

choices.text: Cached replies are reused, so fewer are generated
choices.why: The prompt prefix is cached; every reply is still written.

choices.text: The 5,000-token policy is billed at the cache-read price
choices.why: Right. A repeated prefix is most of each request.

choices.text: Batch prices apply automatically to cached prompts
choices.why: Batch is a separate column with its own conditions.

choices.text: The output price falls when the input is cached
choices.why: The output is billed the same.

prompt: A workload sends 400 requests a day for 30 days, each with 1,000 input tokens at $1 per million and 100 output tokens at $5 per million. What does it cost a month, in dollars?
Which of ana's tasks fits batch prices, and which does not?

choices.text: Drafting fits, because replies are long
choices.why: An agent is waiting for the draft.

choices.text: Neither: batch is only for evaluation
choices.why: Evaluation is one good use, not the only one.

choices.text: Both, since batch halves every bill in the sheet
choices.why: Halving the bill is no use if the answer arrives hours late for a waiting person.

choices.text: A backlog fits; a waiting agent does not
choices.why: Right. Batch suits work nobody is waiting on.

prompt: With streaming, which latency does a person waiting on a draft feel first?
hint: How long the screen stays blank.

choices.text: Time to the whole reply
choices.why: With streaming, text appears before the end.

choices.text: Time to first token
choices.why: Right. Until it arrives the screen is blank.

choices.text: The provider's average over all its customers
choices.why: She feels her own requests, not an average.

choices.text: The time to count the tokens beforehand
choices.why: Counting is a separate, optional call.

prompt: Why does section 06 report the p95 as well as the median?

choices.text: The p95 is always twice the median
choices.why: The ratio varies; in the capture it ranged widely.

choices.text: Providers bill each account by its p95, not by tokens
choices.why: Billing is per token.

choices.text: Slow requests are remembered; a median hides them
choices.why: Right. A tool that is slow one time in twenty loses trust.

choices.text: The median cannot be computed from a stream
choices.why: It was computed from the same timings.

prompt: Section 06's table shows standin-local slowest. What may ana conclude about real self-hosted models from it?

choices.text: Nothing: the course set those speeds; the method is what carries over
choices.why: Right. Measure the real candidates, from where the program runs.

choices.text: That self-hosting is always slower than an API
choices.why: Speed depends on hardware, model and load, none of which the stand-in measured.

choices.text: That a 4-bit model is about one second slower
choices.why: The stand-in has no bits to quantise.

choices.text: That local models have a longer tail
choices.why: The tail came from a factor the course added.

prompt: A prompt of 200,000 tokens is sent at $1 per million input tokens. What does the input cost, in dollars, for one request?
Why does retrieval still matter when many models accept a million tokens?

choices.text: Because a million tokens only counts English text
choices.why: Tokens count text in any language.

choices.text: Because large windows are only available in batch
choices.why: They are offered for normal requests too.

choices.text: Because providers forbid filling the window
choices.why: Filling it is allowed and billed.

choices.text: Every token is paid for and slows the start, and the middle is used less reliably
choices.why: Right. Sending the relevant page beats sending the whole book.

prompt: The sheet's column for the most a model will write in one reply is max ___ tokens.
DeepSeek V3.2 shows no S in the sheet. What does ana do for the extraction task?
hint: A sheet's silence is a question.

choices.text: Keep it, since the sheet is often incomplete
choices.why: Incomplete is a reason to check, not to assume yes.

choices.text: Drop it for extraction until confirmed
choices.why: Right. For a threshold, unrecorded counts as no until checked.

choices.text: Drop it for all three tasks
choices.why: Sorting and drafting do not need structured output.

choices.text: Rank it last on price
choices.why: It is one of the cheapest; price is not the question.

prompt: Every candidate is cheap for Lantern Books. Which column will decide the choice?

choices.text: The window, because larger is safer
choices.why: Every candidate already passes it by a mile.

choices.text: The price, because the cheapest wins
choices.why: Only among those that clear the quality floor.

choices.text: Accuracy on her own cases
choices.why: Right. Lesson 5 fills it.

choices.text: Whether the terms have been read
choices.why: That is a threshold every row already passes.

prompt: Put the steps of section 02's method in order.
items: Filter the sheet on the ones it records
Choose a short list by judgement
Rank the survivors on the trade-offs
trap: Measuring comes before ranking, because the quality floor is itself a threshold.

prompt: Which of these belong in a monthly cost for ana's drafting task? Choose all that apply.
hint: Section 05's three columns and what they assume.

choices.text: The policy tokens, at the cache-read price where caching applies
choices.why: Yes: the repeated prefix is most of each request.

choices.text: The full price for requests that miss the cache
choices.why: Yes: the cached column is a floor for that reason.

choices.text: The reply's tokens at the output price
choices.why: Yes, a small share here but always present.

choices.text: The batch discount
choices.why: An agent is waiting; batch does not apply.
